why: B5 in the relative cell, with an efference copy. The sensor (gain 20) holds the wall near one resting level in all daylight (sum ~0.7-1.3) and silences it in the dark. F (fast, tau 2) and SL (slow, tau 300) read the wall's uniform sum with the same weight and bias, so F - SL is the light's elevation above its level over the last ~5 minutes, at any brightness. R (self 5, bias -2.6: on above ~0.26, off below ~-0.06 on its input 8 (F - SL)) runs the front half (spokes -2 + 8 cos theta, ~0.75 v_max). The run adds a constant ~3.6 to the wall's sum at every daylight level (calculated: 3.54-3.60), so R subtracts its own effect from F and SL (-7.2 each = 2 x 3.6): F - SL keeps reading the light during the run. So R runs while the light keeps rising and stops when it does not (B5). Noise near R's threshold fires exploring runs in dim light; bright steady light is quiet, so the cell parks. Darkness reads as dark, so nights are still. No aim yet.
